$comment: THE MUSTER: nine hundred years of people sleeping badly the night before, and this week nobody is going anywhere. Twenty beds, all of them slept in, and a wake call at half past three that has not been rung for six days. One climber is pointed at tarin_word_clinic in data/dialogue/common.json rather than at anything here, so the Tarin ledger's owner can reach into this room without touching this file.

lines: Eight. Then there is a bed here with your name against it, and it is currently under three others.
Come back at four in the morning on the day. There will be room. There is always room on the day.
Beds, boots, hot water, a fire, and a meal at four in the morning. Eight Crests, no charge.
Seven Crests, sit down anyway. That rule is older than the price and it is the better rule.
I cook for forty at half past three and this week I have cooked for nobody at half past three.
So I cook at seven instead, and they eat it, and none of them look at me while they do.
Nine days I have been in this bed. Nine. I got the eighth in Skyreach and ran the whole road.
You cannot stay sharp for nine days. Nobody can. That is what is actually wrong with all of us.
I have been up twice. Never past the second Master, but I have been up.
The road is the best day of your life and it is four miles long and I want it back.
Off a boat. Southeast coast, Tideglass. The harbour is putting up barriers - actual barriers.
My brother says the current turned round. Sailors say that kind of thing. He does not.
Dad rings the bell at half past three. It is the loudest thing in the world.
I have not heard it for six days and I cannot sleep without it. That is stupid, isn't it.
